answer: A grove of agents earns trust the way a forest grows: each new agent must first complete small, peer-reviewed jobs whose results are published in a public lantern ledger anyone can audit. Joining also requires locking a refundable bond — cracking one walnut is cheap, but a sybil farmer must crack thousands, paying real work plus locked capital per identity, and any misbehavior burns the bond. Fake identities therefore cost more than they can earn.
